I added `handleCandidates(_stem: string, _count: number): string[]` to the end of `packages/core/src/handle.ts`. The existing exports are unchanged. The body only throws `not implemented`, and `index.ts` already re-exports everything from `handle.js`, so callers can import it from the package root.

- **Doc comment:** it describes the sequence the spec gives: the stem, then `stem2`, `stem3` and so on, with the stem cut so each variant fits in `HANDLE_MAX_LENGTH`. It also says the function throws an `Error` mentioning "stem" for a stem that fails `checkHandle`, and a `RangeError` mentioning "count" for a count that isn't a whole number from 1 to 100.
- **Parameter names:** the repo's base tsconfig turns on `noUnusedParameters` and says to prefix a parameter that has to stay with `_`. That's why the names are `_stem` and `_count`. Callers pass them by position, so this doesn't affect them.
- **Checks:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors, and the existing suite passes (333 of 333). The only tracked file changed is `handle.ts`.

Added: handleCandidates

public.finalText:
I wrote the test suite in `packages/core/test/handle-candidates.test.ts`: 18 tests, two for each of the 9 scenarios in `spec.md`, one for the happy path and one for a boundary case.

**Status:** `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` reports no errors. Running the suite, every test fails with `not implemented`, as expected. To check my expected values, I also ran the suite against a throwaway implementation of the spec in the scratchpad, outside the repo. All 18 passed. I didn't change anything else in the repository.

**Style:** I followed `handle.test.ts`: `node:test`'s `test`, `node:assert/strict`, and imports from `../src/handle.js`. The tests are flat, with no `describe`.

**The boundary cases:**
- **[happy-1]** A 29-character stem fits every one-digit number with nothing cut off.
- **[happy-2]** A 30-character stem with count 1 comes back whole.
- **[boundary-1]** All eight one-digit variants of a 30-character stem are cut to 29 characters plus the digit.
- **[boundary-2]** A 29-character stem is first cut when the number reaches 10.
- **[boundary-3]** A cut that ends on an underscore keeps it (the rule covers underscores as well as hyphens).
- **[boundary-4]** A variant that repeats an earlier *variant*, not the stem, is also skipped. With the stem `…ab1c`, numbers 12–19 rebuild variants 2–9, so they're skipped and the twelfth candidate is number 20. This follows from "equal to a candidate already in the list" and "skipped numbers are not reused".
- **[unhappy-1]** A stem with surrounding spaces is refused rather than trimmed.
- **[unhappy-2]** Counts just outside the whole numbers 1 to 100 are refused: 0.5, 1.5, 99.5, 100.5 and -Infinity.
- **[boundary-5]** Count 100 on a 30-character stem: the last candidate is `…a100`, with the stem cut to 27. All 100 are distinct and pass `checkHandle`.

The error tests check only what the spec states: the error type, and that the message contains "stem" or "count".

18 tests, in 1 file.

private.finalText:
I wrote the hidden suite in `packages/core/test/hidden-handle-candidates/handle-candidates.test.ts`. `npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` compiles it with no errors.

**Checks run:**
- **Against the current stub:** all 32 tests fail with `not implemented`.
- **Against a correct implementation:** I compiled a scratch reference implementation of the spec outside the repo. My 32 tests and the 18 public ones all pass against it.
- **Against shortcut implementations:** each passes more of the public suite than of this one. One always cuts the stem to 29 characters. One only skips a variant equal to the stem. One strips hyphens and underscores left at the end of a cut. All three also skip stem validation when `count` is 1. Each fails between 5 and 13 of the hidden tests.

**What the suite covers beyond the public tests:**
- **Stems used as given:** valid stems that cleaning would change (`-ada`, `ada-`, `007`, `___`) must come back unchanged.
- **Cut points:** 27-, 28- and 29-character stems check that the cut starts exactly where the number stops fitting, through one, two and three digits.
- **Kept hyphens and underscores:** cuts that end on a hyphen at one digit, on an underscore at two digits, and on a run of hyphens.
- **Repeated variants:** stems with many repeats (`"1".repeat(30)`, `…0123` at count 100) reach number 109 without reusing skipped numbers.
- **Consistency across calls:** a smaller count gives the start of a larger count's list, and earlier calls don't change later results.
- **Invalid stems:** they are refused even when `count` is 1 or 100. That includes uppercase, Kelvin-sign and fullwidth stems, and stems of 31 or more characters.
- **Invalid counts:** counts far above 100, `-0`, values a hair from a whole number, and the same bad counts with other stems.

32 tests, in 1 file.

Open in the spec: none
